title: EXCLUSIVE: Sequoia-backed chip startup Nuvacore raising funds at about a $2.5 billion valuation, sources say
source_used: Reuters text as carried by Devdiscourse and ET CIO (the Reuters page returned 401)
key_facts: Six-month-old chip start-up Nuvacore, with no product yet, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation, per two people familiar with the fundraising.
The goal is a new central processor (CPU) for data centers.
The round has not closed and the people cautioned that the valuation and size could change.
The Information previously reported that Nuvacore was raising $200 million or more.
Nuvacore is San Jose-based and was founded by Gerard Williams, John Bruno and Ram Srinivasan; Williams sold Nuvia to Qualcomm for $1.4 billion in 2021.
Sequoia Capital led an earlier seed round; Nuvacore declined to comment.
Intel and AMD have long dominated data center CPUs; CPUs act as traffic controllers for Nvidia AI chips and run AI agents.
quote_evidence: Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising.
The funding round has not closed, and the people cautioned that the valuation and size of the capital raise could change.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors are paying billion-dollar prices for AI chip start-ups before they have a product.
notes: Reuters page blocked; text read on Devdiscourse (auto-syndicated Reuters feed) and ET CIO. The article says $10.7 billion went into semiconductor start-ups in the first five months of 2026 and calls that "already outpacing" $12.2 billion for all of 2025, which is internally inconsistent, so that figure was left out.
